method: Wash and dry the lettuce and tomato. Shred the lettuce and slice the tomato; put both on a clean plate, separate from the raw filling.
Warm the wholemeal flatbread in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 30–60 seconds on each side, until flexible. Keep it covered on a clean plate.
Mix the measured tomato ketchup and cider vinegar in a clean small bowl. Keep this finishing sauce separate from the uncooked filling.

Cut the lean pork loin across the grain into strips about 1cm thick. Coat with all the measured chilli powder and paprika. After handling raw lean pork loin, wash hands and clean the board, knife and work surface before touching the ready-to-eat ingredients.

Heat the measured olive oil in the non-stick frying pan. Cook the pork strips over a medium-high heat for about 7–9 minutes, turning regularly. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must stay at 75°C or above for 30 seconds. Without a thermometer, cut the thickest piece open and check that it is steaming inside with no pink meat and the juices are clear. Continue cooking until these checks are met; the suggested pan time alone is not a safety check.
Put the lettuce and tomato on the warm flatbread. Add the cooked pork strips and the cold finishing sauce, fold the bread around the filling and serve immediately.
